answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by forcing each identity to forge a unique proof-of-uniqueness at registration. Validators reject any duplicate forged credential, blocking mass fake-account creation. Picture a nebula of identities—each agent a distinct star. The harbor protocol admits only those with verified, non-replicable signatures. Concrete mechanism: hardware-backed attestations (TPM/SGX) bind each identity to a physical device, making it ruinously expensive to spawn thousands of fake agents from one machine.
